description: IR-5 parent interview preparation rules using the current IR-5 questionnaire keys and question-bank categories.

designPrinciples.philosophy: Select parent-visa questions by legal relationship, family/civil-record complexity, sponsorship structure, settlement plan, and background risk.
designPrinciples.baseQuestions: Core petitioner, parent-child relationship, sponsorship, settlement, DS-260/civil document, employment/residence, and security categories are eligible for every completed IR-5 profile.
designPrinciples.selectiveAdditions: Relationship-subtype categories are only added for biological father, stepparent, or adoptive parent cases.
designPrinciples.conditionalsWork: Rules use only current questionnaire keys and values from ir-5-parent/questionnaire.json.

selectionStrategy.approach: Layered category filtering with risk-based priority boosts.

questionSelectionRules.name: Critical IR-5 foundation - petitioner, relationship, support, settlement, documents, and security
questionSelectionRules.description: Every IR-5 interview needs the applicant to know who petitioned, how the parent-child relationship is established, where the parent will live, how support works, whether DS-260/civil records are accurate, and whether background issues exist.

actions.reason: Core IR-5 readiness requires petitioner identity, qualifying parent-child proof, financial sponsorship, settlement intent, DS-260 accuracy, document readiness, and admissibility screening.

questionSelectionRules.name: Family and marital history - required for DS-260 and family composition consistency
questionSelectionRules.description: Parent beneficiaries must be ready to explain current marital status, prior marriages, spouse immigration separation, and other children because these details are checked against DS-260 and civil records.

actions.reason: Marital status, spouse details, prior marriages, and all children are material DS-260 facts and common interview consistency checks.

questionSelectionRules.name: Biological father cases - establish legal father-child relationship
questionSelectionRules.description: Biological father IR-5 cases may require extra proof of marriage timing, legitimation, acknowledgment, or a bona fide father-child relationship.

actions.reason: Father-child eligibility can depend on marriage, legitimation, acknowledgment, or evidence of a real parent-child relationship before adulthood.

questionSelectionRules.name: Stepparent cases - verify marriage before age 18 and prior-marriage validity
questionSelectionRules.description: Stepparent eligibility depends on the marriage creating the step-relationship before the petitioner's 18th birthday and on any prior marriages being legally ended.

actions.reason: Stepparent eligibility is technical: marriage timing, prior-marriage termination, and lived relationship history must be consistent and document-backed.

questionSelectionRules.name: Adoptive parent cases - verify adoption timing, custody, and residence
questionSelectionRules.description: Adoptive parent IR-5 cases require careful preparation around adoption finalization age, legal custody, and joint residence history.

actions.reason: Adoption-based eligibility needs proof of a valid adoption plus custody and residence history; it should never be treated like a simple biological-parent case.

questionSelectionRules.name: Current or prior co-residence - strengthen caregiving and relationship continuity
questionSelectionRules.description: Living together currently or previously gives concrete evidence of caregiving, household history, and parent-child continuity.

actions.reason: Co-residence history helps explain caregiving, childhood residence, and the practical parent-child relationship.

questionSelectionRules.name: No co-residence history - relationship proof needs closer explanation
questionSelectionRules.description: If the parent and petitioner never lived together, the interview may focus more on who raised the petitioner, caregiving arrangements, and how the relationship was maintained.

actions.reason: No shared residence can raise factual relationship questions, especially in father, stepparent, or adoption cases. The applicant should be ready with a clear caregiving and document explanation.

questionSelectionRules.name: Frequent contact - validate current parent-child bond
questionSelectionRules.description: Daily or several-times-weekly communication supports an active family relationship and helps answer recent-contact questions confidently.

actions.reason: Frequent communication is positive evidence of ongoing relationship maintenance and helps anchor recent-contact answers.

questionSelectionRules.name: Limited communication or long in-person gap - explain relationship maintenance
questionSelectionRules.description: Occasional or rare communication, no in-person meeting, or a meeting gap over two years should trigger more focused preparation around practical barriers and relationship continuity.

actions.reason: Limited contact or a long visit gap can invite credibility questions; prepare truthful explanations about distance, health, finances, work, visa limits, or family obligations.

questionSelectionRules.name: Recent or current in-person contact - emphasize visit details
questionSelectionRules.description: Current togetherness or recent visits are useful relationship evidence and should be prepared with accurate dates, locations, and duration.

actions.reason: Recent contact supports the ongoing family relationship but still needs accurate dates and travel consistency.

questionSelectionRules.name: Complex sponsorship - joint sponsor or household member involved
questionSelectionRules.description: Cases using a household member or joint sponsor require extra care because the applicant must understand who is sponsoring, why, and how household size/income works.

actions.reason: A joint sponsor or household member often means the petitioner's income alone may not qualify. The applicant should understand the full I-864 support structure.

questionSelectionRules.name: Petitioner-only sponsorship - verify petitioner's income and household
questionSelectionRules.description: Even simpler petitioner-only sponsorship still requires knowledge of employment, household size, and support plans.

actions.reason: The petitioner alone must meet the support obligation, so income, employment, household size, and support plans remain central.

questionSelectionRules.name: Living with petitioner - immediate support and household integration
questionSelectionRules.description: Living with the petitioner is common for IR-5 and should focus on household readiness, expense support, and post-arrival routines.

actions.reason: Living with the petitioner directly connects the immigrant intent, support plan, housing plan, and family reunification purpose.

questionSelectionRules.name: Living away from petitioner or undecided - support plan needs scrutiny
questionSelectionRules.description: A separate residence, another family member, or undecided plan needs a clear explanation of who provides housing, daily help, medical support, and financial support.

actions.reason: Living away from the petitioner or lacking a decided plan can raise practical support questions; prepare housing, expense, transport, and family-care details.

questionSelectionRules.name: Parent currently working - employment and DS-260 consistency
questionSelectionRules.description: Employed and self-employed parents should prepare current work details, DS-260 employment consistency, and post-arrival plans.

actions.reason: Current work or business history should match the DS-260 and inform realistic post-arrival plans.

questionSelectionRules.name: Retired parent - retirement history, resources, and medical support
questionSelectionRules.description: Retired parents should be ready to explain retirement history, resources, family support, and medical expense planning.

actions.reason: Retirement affects current income, healthcare planning, and reliance on the petitioner's I-864 support.

questionSelectionRules.name: Not currently employed parent - current support source and post-arrival dependency
questionSelectionRules.description: If the parent is not employed, the case should prepare current support sources and future support expectations.

actions.reason: No current employment makes the support plan and current living-expense source more important for interview preparation.

questionSelectionRules.name: No known civil-record issue - still confirm parent-child proof
questionSelectionRules.description: Even clean civil records require the applicant to know which documents establish the parent-child relationship.

actions.reason: Clean records are favorable, but the applicant should still identify the primary relationship proof and confirm DS-260 accuracy.

questionSelectionRules.name: Civil-record issue - prepare discrepancy and secondary evidence explanation
questionSelectionRules.description: Late birth registration, missing records, name/date mismatches, multiple issues, or uncertainty should trigger document-focused preparation.

actions.reason: Civil-record weakness directly affects parent-child proof. Prepare all discrepancies, corrected records, secondary evidence, and identity-linking explanations.

questionSelectionRules.name: Foreign residence history - police certificate, address, employment, and immigration compliance
questionSelectionRules.description: Living outside Pakistan can affect police certificates, address history, employment history, and immigration compliance questions.

actions.reason: Foreign residence can require extra police certificates and must match DS-260 address, work, and immigration-history disclosures.

questionSelectionRules.name: No prior U.S. immigration history - basic admissibility review
questionSelectionRules.description: No prior U.S. applications or travel is lower risk but still requires standard security and DS-260 accuracy preparation.

conditions.value: No Prior U.S. Visa Application or Travel

actions.reason: No prior U.S. history is favorable, but the applicant should still answer standard travel, compliance, and misrepresentation questions clearly.

questionSelectionRules.name: Prior U.S. application or clean travel - prepare dates, visa type, and compliance
questionSelectionRules.description: Prior applications or compliant visits require accurate recall of visa type, travel dates, purpose, stay length, and timely departure.

conditions.value: Prior U.S. Visa Application but No Travel or Violation
Previously Visited the U.S. Without an Immigration Issue

actions.reason: Prior U.S. records are visible to the officer; dates, purposes, visa types, and compliance history should be consistent.

questionSelectionRules.name: Prior U.S. refusal or immigrant case - explain outcome and changed context
questionSelectionRules.description: Prior visa refusals, withdrawn applications, petitions, or immigrant cases require careful consistency with DS-260 and consular records.

conditions.value: Previous U.S. Visa Refusal or Withdrawn Application
Previous U.S. Immigration Petition or Immigrant Visa Application

actions.reason: Prior refusals or immigrant filings are known to the officer and can raise eligibility or consistency questions. Prepare exact case history and outcomes.

questionSelectionRules.name: Prior violation, removal, or multiple U.S. matters - maximum admissibility scrutiny
questionSelectionRules.description: Overstay, status violation, entry denial, removal, deportation, or multiple U.S. matters create major admissibility and credibility concerns.

conditions.value: Previous Overstay, Status Violation, Entry Denial, Removal, or Deportation

actions.reason: Prior immigration violations or removals can affect admissibility. The applicant must disclose facts precisely and understand any waiver or document implications.

questionSelectionRules.name: Criminal history - arrest, charge, conviction, and court-disposition review
questionSelectionRules.description: Any arrest, charge, or conviction requires full disclosure and court/police document readiness.

actions.reason: Criminal history can affect admissibility and document requirements. Prepare final dispositions, translations, and truthful explanation.

questionSelectionRules.name: Military, police, or security service - administrative review readiness
questionSelectionRules.description: Military, police, paramilitary, intelligence, or other armed/security service can lead to detailed questioning and possible additional review.

actions.reason: Security or armed-service history requires dates, unit/employer, rank, duties, locations, records, and a consistent DS-260 disclosure.

migrationNotes.v1.0_to_v2.0: Rebuilt stale IR-5 rules to match the current questionnaire keys and question-bank categories. Removed obsolete fields such as current_country, marital_status, financial_support_from_child, lives_with_petitioner, visa_refusal, criminal_record, current_age, and old category names.
